messages:
support-oncall: Customer ACME (acct: acme-corp) opened INC-4321 — p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~320ms -> ~1.8s starting ~02:00 UTC. Impacting europe-1 region. Any known rollouts or recent infra changes?

maya: ACKing, investigating. Can you paste request IDs or a sample trace?

support-oncall: added a couple request IDs in the ticket: r-3f9a, r-3fa2. They show long backend time not network. No customer-side changes.

sam: quick telemetry: p95 went 350ms -> 700ms, p99 went 320ms -> 1.8s. KV/prefix-cache miss rate jumped at 02:03 UTC on all europe-1 hosts. Metrics snippet: 
```
kv_prefix_miss_rate  (host-avg): 0.13 -> 0.47
kv_evictions_per_sec : 5 -> 220
kv_warmups_pending   : 0 -> 14
```
Also saw lots of prefix cache churn and >90% of miss firings for model: text-redwood-v2-large.

priya: interesting — we merged the request-key-normalization change yesterday to dedupe some dynamic headers. That PR normalized query params and removed a hashing step that used route-prefix. Could be we dramatically increased key entropy for prefix cache.

maya: can you point to the exact change? If keys now include volatile request-id params we will get near-zero prefix reuse.

priya: snippet from PR 948: 
```
- cache_key = f"{model}:{route}:{hash(params)}"
+ cache_key = f"{model}:{route}:{params}"  # removed hash to keep readable
```
So we stopped hashing param blobs. For small param variability that would explode cache keys.

jonathan: that matches the evictions spike. Hot prefixes spilled because the cache slot mapping is based on normalized keys. Without hashing, the prefix bucket index distribution became very sparse. TLDR: key entropy up -> miss rate up -> KV warmup thrash -> p99 tail.

maya: immediate mitigations? Customer SLA is impacted.

jonathan: propose 3-step plan: 
1) revert PR 948 (fast rollback) to restore hashed compact keys (hotfix)
2) temporarily increase prefix-cache capacity on europe-1 pools (scale config) to absorb current working set while we patch (eg +50% entries)
3) throttle low-priority background warmups and enable sticky routing to warm hosts for Acme's requests to avoid cold starts.

lee: I already created a canary revert branch and started a canary rollout to 2 instances in europe-1. Command I used: 
```
# deploy canary
deploy-bot rollback --service=kv-prefix-cache --revision=pr-947-canary --region=europe-1 --instances=2
```
Monitoring now: see reduced misses on canary host.

sam: also added a temporary config to eviction policy to favor LRU across prefix buckets to reduce cross-bucket thrash: 
```
kv.eviction_policy = "lru_global"
kv.max_entries = kv.max_entries * 1.5
```
This is a hot config change on the config service, will persist until we validate.

support-oncall: looped in customer with ETA ~45m for an initial mitigation. They asked for root cause and a timeline for full fix.

maya: QA checklist before full revert rollout: 
- confirm canary p99 drop (sam)
- run synthetic load reproducer hitting the same param patterns (priya)
- ensure telemetry doesn't regress memory usage (lee)

priya: created repro script for local testing: 
```
# repro: generate many keys with high param entropy
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://eu1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"text-redwood-v2-large","prompt":"hi","request_id":"'$RANDOM'"}' &
done
```
This triggers the same miss pattern locally. Verified that hashed-key implementation reduces unique cache keys by ~95%.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: revert-948 -> 40% europe-1 (2/5), expected completion 15m.

maya: logging note: add a short-lived debug flag to record `cache_key` samples for affected requests (rotate after 1h). This will help confirm keys include volatile fields.

jonathan: longer-term: reintroduce readable keys but keep a stable hashing layer for high-card fields. Also add unit tests to block non-hashed high-entropy params and a metric for unique-key-cardinality per model-route.

lee: post-mitigation checklist: 
- monitor kv_prefix_miss_rate, kv_evictions_per_sec, p99 for 30m window
- if stable, roll revert to 100% and remove temporary eviction config
- follow up with a PR that implements hash+stable-salt with a migration plan

support-oncall: customer updated: we applied a mitigation and are monitoring. They'll keep the ticket open for RCA. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maya: wrapping up — action items assigned: 
- priya: open PR to revert + add tests (assigned)
- jonathan: run capacity increase + rollback plan (assigned)
- sam: watch SLOs and update incident channel (assigned)
- lee: validate memory impact and eviction metrics (assigned)
- maya: draft apology + RCA template for ACME (assigned)

support-oncall: closing loop — will update INC-4321 as we get more telemetry.
